plan.title: Entropy: Why Hot Coffee Never Reheats Itself
plan.description: Entropy measures how spread out energy is, and the second law says it never decreases in an isolated system. This explains why some processes are irreversible.

beats.narration: Your coffee always cools down. It never heats itself back up. The reason has a name: entropy.

props.text: Coffee cools. It never reheats itself.

beats.narration: Entropy measures how spread out energy is. Low entropy means energy is concentrated in one place. High entropy means it is dispersed evenly.
The second law of thermodynamics says that in an isolated system, entropy cannot decrease. Everything drifts toward equilibrium, where entropy is highest.

props.text: In an isolated system, entropy never decreases.

beats.narration: That is why some processes are irreversible. Heat flows out, energy spreads, and time has a direction. Entropy is the universe spreading itself out.
